stem.text: Compound Y is heated with a mild oxidising agent. One of the products of the reaction reacts with hydrogen cyanide, forming 2-hydroxybutanenitrile.

explanation.text: Work backwards from the product name. In a nitrile the C≡N carbon is C1 of the chain, so 2-hydroxybutanenitrile, CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH(OH)CN, has four carbons including the CN carbon. HCN adds one carbon, so the carbonyl compound has three carbons with the C=O at the chain end: propanal, CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CHO.
Propanal is made by mild oxidation (with distillation) of the primary alcohol propan-1-ol.

optionAnalysis.text: Butan-1-ol oxidises to butanal; adding HCN would give a five-carbon product, 2-hydroxypentanenitrile.
Butan-2-ol oxidises to butanone; adding HCN gives 2-hydroxy-2-methylbutanenitrile, a five-carbon branched product.
Propan-1-ol oxidises to propanal, and CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CHO + HCN → CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH(OH)CN, 2-hydroxybutanenitrile.
Propan-2-ol oxidises to propanone; adding HCN gives 2-hydroxy-2-methylpropanenitrile, not a straight-chain product.

reasoningChain: 2-hydroxybutanenitrile = CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH(OH)CN (4 C, counting the CN carbon).
HCN adds the CN carbon, so the carbonyl compound has 3 C: CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CHO, propanal.
Propanal comes from mild oxidation of propan-1-ol.

inferredMistakes.text: Matching the “butane” in the product name directly to a butanol, forgetting that the CN carbon comes from HCN.
Choosing a secondary alcohol, whose ketone would put the OH and CN on a carbon that also carries two alkyl groups.

issues: ER 原文自相矛盾：第一条写 “Option C was a common incorrect answer.”，第二条结论和 MS 都是 C 正确。按原文照抄未改，疑似 ER 把常见错选项写错（可能是 A，即 butan-1-ol），请审核。

bullets: Option C was a common incorrect answer.

The compound that reacts with hydrogen cyanide, forming 2-hydroxybutanenitrile, is propanal.

CH3CH2CHO + HCN → CH3CH2CH(OH)CN

Therefore propanal is produced when compound Y undergoes mild oxidation. Compound Y must be propan-1-ol. The correct option is C.
